title: Odd Days, Even Days
subject: Sixty-year-old identical twin brothers own one old bicycle between them and ride it on alternate dates, odd days for one and even days for the other, until the 31st of the month starts an argument.
caption: Baroque pop, gentle 4/4 lilt with a walking bassline. Bright harpsichord playing broken-chord figures, a string quartet with sweeping legato cello and violin countermelodies, felt piano doubling the vocal, a solo flute answering the chorus, soft brushed snare and round electric bass. 1967 London studio texture, plate reverb, warm tape saturation, strings forward. Male lead, light clear tenor, intimate mid register, tender delivery with close double-tracked harmony on the chorus. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 92 BPM, D major. Wistful, tender, gently comic. No drum machine, no electric guitar distortion, no synth pads, no autotune, no modern pop production.
lyrics:
[Intro - harpsichord figure, then cello and flute enter]

[Verse 1]
One old bicycle, two grey men
Same chin, same cough, same walk back then
Odd days Edwin, even days me
That's the deal we signed at seventy-three

[Chorus]
Odd days, even days, we take our turns
Twin of mine, I'll wait at the gate
He leaves a note in the basket each night
"Mind the left brake, it pulls to the right"

[Verse 2]
Thirty-one comes round like a bill
Whose turn is it? Neither of us will
Say it's his, so we both stand still
Two old brothers at the foot of the hill

[Chorus]
Odd days, even days, we take our turns
Twin of mine, I'll wait at the gate
I hear his bell come up the lane
My turn to wait, my turn again

[Bridge - strings alone, harpsichord rolling]
Two shadows on one wheel
Going round the way they feel

[Chorus]
Odd days, even days, we take our turns
But the thirty-first, we ride it together
Him on the saddle and me on the bar
Twin of mine, it isn't far

[Outro - flute and harpsichord, strings fade]
Odd days, even days
One bicycle, two ways
